title: On Separation Axioms, Compactness, Metrizability, and Quotient Constructions for Bitopological Gyrogroups
content: We investigate separation axioms, compactness, metrizability, and quotient constructions for bitopological gyrogroups. A bitopological gyrogroup is a gyrogroup equipped with two topologies, each of which makes the gyrogroup operation and inversion continuous. We distinguish the separation properties of the individual topologies from pairwise separation properties of the associated bitopological space. We establish elementary results concerning Hausdorffness, compactness, continuous homomorphisms, and metrizability. We also study quotient topologies induced by compatible equivalence relations and explain conditions under which a quotient carries a well-defined gyrogroup structure. The distinction between a quotient space and a quotient gyrogroup is emphasized. The results are related to established work on topological and strongly topological gyrogroups, particularly the study of metrizability and quotient spaces. Several questions concerning simultaneous separation properties, compactness, and metrizability for two compatible topologies are proposed.
